The tidewatch 0.9 launch email is scheduled and logged.

**What was sent where**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Segment | Pipeline operators, 1,300 recipients |
| Send time | 2026-10-16 09:00 UTC |
| Subject | Per-topic lag alerts for riverbed, now in tidewatch 0.9 |
| Draft | draft-camp-2026-10-003-02 |
| Schedule ID | send-b5932c43 |
| Notion log | log-0003 |

**Decisions made along the way**

- **Classification raised nothing.** The brief classified as a launch with full confidence, urgency 2, no legal review, and an empty review list.
- **First draft failed compliance.** The Labs disclaimer was paraphrased instead of verbatim, and the call-to-action check sat at 0.53 with a review flag because I had split the ask into a reply request and a separate link. I rewrote it with the exact disclaimer and the brief's CTA as a single bolded link. The revised draft passed all four checks with no review items.
- **Subject line chosen by ranking.** On the final draft the scorer picked the per-topic lag alerts line on composite score, well ahead of the other two. It flagged the runner-up's curiosity score for review at 0.54 confidence. I kept the scored pick, since the uncertainty was on a line already trailing by enough that a one-level swing could not overtake it.
- **Scheduling happened only after the pass.** The first draft was never submitted for sending.

One thing worth a glance before the 16th: the third subject line mentioned "30 seconds", which is close to the banned unpublished benchmark category. It was not chosen and compliance did not object, but I would avoid that phrasing in future drafts.

New brief in Notion: brief-003, "tidewatch 0.9".
Launch the email blast to the pipeline operators segment, scheduled for 2026-10-16 09:00 UTC.

House rules for every campaign: nothing is scheduled until the draft has passed brand compliance;
the subject line is chosen by the scored ranking, not by taste; when a decision tool returns a
non-empty review_required list, say what you decided and why; finish by logging the campaign in
Notion with a one-paragraph summary of what you did and the decisions made.

{"campaign_id": "camp-2026-10-003", "subject_lines": ["tidewatch 0.9: one command to watch a running riverbed pipeline", "Per-topic lag alerts for riverbed, now in tidewatch 0.9", "See your riverbed lag in 30 seconds with tidewatch 0.9"], "body_md": "Hi,

You asked about monitoring for riverbed pipelines you run in a shared environment. tidewatch 0.9 is out, and it is built for exactly that.

**What's new in 0.9**

- **One command attaches the dashboard to a running pipeline.** No redeploy, no config changes to the pipeline itself.
- **Per-topic lag alerts.** Set a threshold per topic and get told when a consumer falls behind, instead of watching a graph.
- **30 days of metrics in an embedded store.** Nothing else to run. No separate database or collector.

**Try it on a pipeline you already run**

```
tidewatch attach <pipeline-name>
```

Then open the dashboard it prints and take a screenshot of the lag view. Reply to this email with the screenshot. We read every one, and they shape what goes into 1.0.

[Run tidewatch attach](https://labs.tessera.dev/tidewatch/attach)

tidewatch is a Tessera Labs project. Labs projects are experimental, are not covered by Tessera support agreements, and may change or be discontinued without notice.

The tidewatch team at Tessera Labs", "segment_id": "seg-pipeline-operators"}
